beliefs: f increments the last character of the input by one Unicode code point if it is a letter (any script), before inserting '4' [E1, E2, E3]
f inserts '4' at index len(s)//2 of the (possibly incremented) string [E1, E2, E3]
Non-letter last characters (digits, symbols, spaces) are left unchanged [E1]
Increment wraps within the letter's own case: 'z'→'a', 'Z'→'A', 'é'→'ê', 'É'→'Ê' [E2, E3]
The insertion index is computed from the original string's length, which equals the incremented string's length [E1, E2, E3]
For non-ASCII letters, incrementing is by code point (é→ê), not by case-folding or ASCII-only rules [E3]
